subject: general
question: Which authority decides citizenship for people in newly added territories?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Union Government**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Union Government is responsible for deciding citizenship in newly added territories to India as per the provisions of the Constitution and relevant laws.
 
• **Article 11** of the Indian Constitution **empowers Parliament to regulate the right of citizenship by law.**
 
• The Citizenship Act of 1955, enacted by the Union Government, lays out the legal framework for acquiring, renouncing, and determining citizenship in India.
 
• In cases where new territories are added to India, the Union Government decides citizenship based on the provisions outlined in the Citizenship Act.
 
• International agreements or treaties governing territorial addition may also influence citizenship decisions, which are implemented by the Union Government.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 5-11 of the Indian Constitution:**

 
 
• These articles govern citizenship provisions in India.
 
• Article 11 explicitly empowers Parliament to make laws regulating citizenship.
 
 
 
• **The Citizenship Act, 1955:**
 
 
• It is the primary law governing citizenship in India.
 
• It includes provisions for citizenship by birth, descent, registration, naturalization, and incorporation of territory.
 
 
 
• **Incorporation of Territory:**
 
 
• When a new territory is added to India, its residents may be granted Indian citizenship based on legal provisions.
 
• The Union Government decides the criteria and implementation process for granting citizenship.
 
 
 
• **International Treaties and Agreements:**
 
 
• Territorial additions often occur due to international agreements or treaties.
 
• The Union Government ensures compliance with these agreements while determining citizenship for affected residents.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Oversight:**
 
 
• In case of disputes or challenges, the Supreme Court of India may interpret constitutional provisions related to citizenship.
 
• However, the primary authority remains with the Union Government.
